falsifier: Find an int-to-float conversion site where our stream carries `xoris rX,rX,32768` and the target does not, and where widening the SOURCE CARRIER's declared type to an unsigned 32-bit type leaves the xoris in place; or find one where the target itself emits xoris while our unsigned-carrier form does not, which would show the target used a signed carrier and invert the prescription. The evidence is the pairing of the xoris words with the FPR bias constant subtracted immediately after them: read both with tools/gdl/fnasm.py --diff, since the bias register differs between the two magics and is the independent confirmation that the conversion signedness, not the arithmetic, is what changed.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
A SURPLUS `xoris rX,rX,32768` BEFORE AN INT-TO-FLOAT CONVERSION IS A TYPE-PROMOTION TELL, NOT A CODEGEN QUIRK: THE CARRIER IS NARROWER THAN int, SO ITS MASKED SUB-EXPRESSIONS PROMOTE TO SIGNED int AND MWCC SELECTS THE SIGNED MAGIC. Widening the carrier's declared type to an unsigned 32-bit type selects the unsigned magic and removes the xoris - one per conversion site, all at once.

THE MEASUREMENT. sDrawGeom's `--ops` delta carried `ours-only: -3 xoris` for three runs across two lanes without being localised. Screening the multiset for the mnemonic put all three inside a single three-line block, and the aligned read at +0x9ac showed the shape exactly: our stream is `rlwinm rX,rS,3,24,28 / xoris rX,rX,32768 / stw rX,...` three times over, and subtracts one FPR bias; the target is `rlwinm rD,rS,3,24,28 / stw rD,...` with no xoris, subtracting a DIFFERENT FPR bias. Two magics, distinguishable by the bias register alone. The source was `u16 v2 = pbSwap16(...)` followed by three statements of the form `uv2[k] = (f32)((v2 >> n) & MASK);`. Because v2 is u16, every masked sub-expression has type `int` after integral promotion - signed - so MWCC emits the signed 0x4330000080000000 sequence. Declaring the carrier `u32 v2` makes all three expressions unsigned and reproduces the target's form and bias: insns 1023 -> 1020, multiset 26t -> 23t, real 1180 -> 1177, fuzzy 88.6120 -> 88.8095, in one character class.

WHY IT IS SEMANTICS-PRESERVING AND THEREFORE NOT A FAKEMATCH. Every use is an 8-bit masked quantity, so the value set is identical under either carrier width; only the C type of the intermediate changes. This is a reconstruction IMPROVEMENT rather than debt - a u32 carrier for a swapped 16-bit word is exactly what a 2001 author writing bit-unpacking code would have declared, and the narrow declaration is the artefact.

HOW TO USE IT. Screen for `xoris` in the `--ops` multiset FIRST, before any register or schedule theory: the mnemonic localises to the conversion site by itself, and one carrier-type edit can close every site in the block. Then check the direction - if the TARGET carries the xoris and we do not, the prescription inverts and the target's carrier is the signed one. Do not reach for a `(u32)` cast at each use site: the cast form works but is per-site, is reconstruction debt, and misses that the DECLARATION is what the original author got right.

A COMPANION NEGATIVE FROM THE SAME BLOCK, worth reading before the next narrow-type probe in this family, because it shows the two cheapest predictors agreeing and both being wrong. `kick = ((nv >> 15) & 1) != 0;` was simplified to `kick = (nv >> 15) & 1;` on the reasoning that the comparison is redundant on an already-0/1 value and that our stream carried a surplus `clrlwi` before the byte store. It measured real 1177 -> 1143 and count distance 7 -> 3 - a 34-row gain and a halved count gap - while the multiset went 23t -> 25t and fuzzy fell 88.8095 -> 88.7068. The aligned read showed the edit had DELETED an `addic`/`subfe`/`clrlwi` triple that the target CONTAINS: MWCC really does normalise `!= 0` through the addic/subfe idiom, and the target's source really did write the comparison. GENERAL FORM OF THE DISCRIMINANT, confirmed independently on serve_blits the same session: when `real` and count distance improve while the OPCODE MULTISET WORSENS, the gain is alignment luck and the edit is deleting instructions the target has. The multiset is the finer instrument for that question because it is position-free; real and count distance are not.
